draft.title: The Dreaming
card: For many Aboriginal peoples, the Dreaming is not only a time in the past. It is an ongoing reality that is still present today.
It explains how the world came to be. Ancestral beings shaped the land, waters, animals and people, and their stories are passed on.
It also sets out law, meaning the right ways to live and the duties people hold. It explains kinship, which is how people are related to each other.
It joins people to the land they belong to. Different Aboriginal peoples have their own Dreaming stories, so there is no single Dreaming story shared by all.
draft.remember: The Dreaming is a living reality that gives law, kinship and connection to land, not just stories of the past.

a.q: Which statement best describes how many Aboriginal peoples understand the Dreaming?
opts: An ongoing reality that still shapes life and law today
A single story of creation shared by all Aboriginal peoples
A period long ago that ended once the world was formed
A set of tales told only to entertain children
a.why: The Dreaming is understood as ongoing, so it still shapes law, kinship and connection to land. The tempting option, that it ended after creation, treats it as only a past time, which the card says it is not.
a.clue: Think about whether the Dreaming is finished or still present.

b.q: An Elder tells a young person that the law of how to care for a waterhole comes from the Dreaming. What does this show about the Dreaming?
opts: It still guides how people live and their duties today
It explains how the waterhole formed but sets no rules
It is the same story for every Aboriginal people
It describes events that have no link to present life
b.why: The Elder links a present duty to the Dreaming, so it gives law that still guides people. The second option is tempting because the Dreaming does explain creation, but the card says it also sets out law and duties.
b.clue: The Elder is speaking about a rule for people now.

a.best: An ongoing reality that still shapes life and law today

b.best: It still guides how people live and their duties today
